item.title: Apache Kafka Architecture
item.description:
Simple definition#

Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform. At its core it is a replicated, partitioned, append-only log: producers append records, the cluster stores them durably for a configured time, and any number of consumers read them independently. Each consumer can re-read old records whenever it needs to.

item.title: Kafka Producers, Consumers and Delivery Guarantees
item.description:
Simple definition#

A producer writes records to topic partitions. A consumer reads them and records its progress as offsets. Delivery guarantees describe what happens to a record when something fails in between: it can be lost, duplicated or processed exactly once.

item.title: Event-Driven Architecture
item.description:
Simple definition#

In an event-driven architecture (EDA), services announce facts that happened (“PaymentAuthorised”) instead of telling other services what to do. Interested services react to those events in their own time. The producer does not know, or need to know, who is listening.

item.title: Transactional Outbox, CDC and Idempotent Consumers
item.description:
Simple definition#

  • Transactional outbox: write the business change and the event to the same database in one transaction, then publish the event from the database to the broker.
  • Change data capture (CDC): read a database’s transaction log and stream every change as events.
  • Idempotent consumer: a consumer that gives the same result whether a message arrives once or several times.

Together they give effectively-once processing without distributed transactions.

item.title: Schemas, Event Contracts and Evolution
item.description:
Simple definition#

An event contract is the agreed shape and meaning of an event: field names, types, required fields, semantics and service levels. A schema registry stores every version of that shape and checks that new versions do not break existing producers or consumers.

item.title: System Design: Event-Driven Real-Time Payments
item.description:
The design brief#

“Design the core of a bank’s instant payments service. Customers send money from mobile and web; payments must settle in under 10 seconds, end to end, 24×7. Each payment must be fraud-checked, posted to the ledger exactly once, notified to both parties and reconciled with the scheme daily.”
